policy: flag only - no fixes are applied anywhere in this pipeline
how_to_read: measured.points_to_own_all is the real cost of the combination from a fresh character in the named home zone, using the same engine the UI calls. share_of_career_budget is that cost over the level-20 budget.

flags.title: Multiple Extra Attack sources reachable by one character
flags.raw_position: Extra Attack features from different classes do not stack (2024 PHB, multiclassing).
flags.concern: RAW, Extra Attack from different classes explicitly does not stack, and multiclassing gates it behind class levels. Here every source is a node, and nothing in the data says they are mutually exclusive. A character that walks Fighter and Warlock can hold Two Extra Attacks and Thirsting Blade/Devouring Blade at once.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Two full-caster slot spines reachable by one character
flags.raw_position: Multiclass casters share one pooled slot progression (2024 PHB, multiclass spellcasting).
flags.concern: RAW pools multiclass spell slots into one progression; two separate 9th-level slot tracks is strictly more resource than any RAW character has. The spines are cheap to walk once you are inside a zone, so the only thing stopping this is cross-zone distance.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Heavy armor training combined with monk/barbarian mobility
flags.raw_position: Unarmored Movement requires no armor; Rage requires no Heavy armor.
flags.concern: Monk and Barbarian movement bonuses are RAW-conditional on wearing no armor (Monk) or no Heavy armor (Barbarian Rage). Armor training is now a purchasable core connector, so the conditionality has to be enforced in the rules layer - the tree cannot express it.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Multiple Unarmored Defense calculations available at once
flags.raw_position: Only one Unarmored Defense formula applies at a time.
flags.concern: Barbarian, Monk and College of Dance each define their own AC formula. Owning several does not stack in RAW, but nothing in the node data encodes 'pick the best, not the sum'.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Full Sneak Attack progression alongside Extra Attack
flags.raw_position: Sneak Attack dice scale with Rogue level only.
flags.concern: RAW this costs a rogue their whole level progression; here Sneak Attack scaling lives on the Rogue ladder and Extra Attack on the Fighter ladder, and both are reachable within one career budget.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Rage held together with a full slot progression
flags.raw_position: You cannot cast or concentrate on spells while Raging.
flags.concern: RAW forbids casting or concentrating while Raging, which is a rules restriction rather than an acquisition restriction. Worth confirming the rules layer still enforces it once the tree stops caring about class identity.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Expertise grants from several zones plus Boon of Skill
flags.raw_position: Expertise is granted a fixed number of times per class.
flags.concern: The extraction already cross-links every Expertise feature to every other, so these sit unusually close together in the graph. Skill DCs are the softest part of the maths and the least likely to be checked.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: Every character can buy the Fighter-sized ASI chain
flags.raw_position: ASI slot count varies by class (4 for most, 5 Rogue, 7 Fighter).
flags.concern: The repeat chain is sized to the RAW ceiling (Fighter's seven slots), so a character in any zone can now reach seven ASIs. The 20-point cap per ability still applies, but the spread does not.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

flags.title: More than one level-20 capstone reachable in a career
flags.raw_position: A character reaches exactly one level-20 class feature.
flags.concern: Capstones are designed as the single reward for never multiclassing. Depth is the only thing keeping a player from collecting two, so this is the clearest test of whether RING_STEP and the point budget are tuned correctly.
flags.suggested_review: Compare share_of_career_budget against how much of a build this combination actually is. If it is cheap, push the nodes deeper (Task 4 says depth, not price, is the lever).

resolved_in_review.title: Work Order 1 reference edges bypassed the depth ladder
resolved_in_review.resolution: Marked non-traversable (Work Order 2 review, item 1). edges.json was a citation registry from the extraction, not designed connectivity. The edges stay in the data tagged relation="reference" for future 'see also' UI, and the pathing engine excludes them, so depth remains the sole balance lever under flat costing.

resolved_in_review.title: Pact Magic short-rest recovery is not represented
resolved_in_review.resolution: Out of scope (review, item 3). Recovery timing is character-state tracking, not tree structure; it belongs to a later work order. The Pact Magic chain models acquisition only, deliberately.

resolved_in_review.title: Slot spine nodes cost a point even in your own zone
resolved_in_review.resolution: Correct as implemented (review, item 2). The own-zone exemption skips the connector toll, not the destination node's own price.
